overall_quality.reason: Correct core distinction between compilation and interpretation, though oversimplified (e.g., 'both translate into machine code' is not always true, bytecode/VMs ignored).
overall_quality.evidence: A compiler and an interpreter both translate source code into machine code, but they do so in different ways. A compiler translates the entire program into machine code before execution, while an interpreter translates and executes the code line by line. This means a compiler is faster for large programs but slower for small ones. An interpreter is more flexible and can execute code on the fly, but it's slower overall.
